title: Cultureway document, schema 2
description: One culture as data. Additive over the shipped v1 shape (tools/fixtures/cultures-pig.json); unknown sections are ignored by the engine (forward-compat by construction). Authoritative clamps live in game.js cultureProblem - this schema mirrors them for authoring-time validation and MUST NOT be looser.

traits.description: E2 (census C3): this people's personality table. Multipliers are integer TWENTIETHS (20 = 1.0, clamped 4-60 = 0.2x-3.0x). Key order is the hire draw order. Undeclared = the island's six traits. Each trait must quip all three moments (commute/work/home).

world.description: PLACE art - reserved (accepted and ignored until the renderer exists). Backdrop layers, terrain, building templates, props, lighting.

idle.description: E1: the four idle moments this people quips at - play, gossip, a stroll, waking from a nap. Undeclared moments fall to the island's lines; unknown keys are refused at import (A QUIP FOR NOWHERE).

appeal.description: THE ONE TABLE for what draws this people: standing taste weights and the drop-nudge terms together. Top-level `tastes` is gone; a document that still carries it fails loudly at install.

tastes.description: Per-recipe multiplier, 1.0 when unstated. Below 1 is dislike, 0.1 is effectively taboo.

nudge.description: Drop-nudge terms in AUTHOR units, converted once at install: radius in px, minutes on the game clock, relax quantized to the sim's Q20 grid by the same quantizer the engine's own constant uses, mul100 in appeal's hundredths (130 = x1.3). Fields left out inherit the crab values (72 / 60 / 0.12 / 130).

management.description: The culture's working norms, in AUTHOR units converted once at install. tableTip is what a guest of this people leaves on the table, in whole dollars (crab: 9); counter20 is the jar's token share of that tip at the counter, in twentieths (crab: 3 = the old 0.15); shifts shape their working day in half-hour minutes - std is the M/E standard day (crab: 360), day the owner-operator's open-to-close cap (crab: 600), cover the covering double (crab: 720). Fields left out inherit the crab values. The town's WAGE_STD is deliberately NOT here: it is the town's arithmetic grid, and a culture's customary wage joins this section in the settlers slice, when someone exists to read it.

settlers.description: Phase B (debt items 2-3): may this people STAY? apron: a visitor of this culture accepts a job offer and converts to a resident through the persona factory, keeping her name, face, hat and culture - the settled resident works shifts, draws wages and sleeps in town housing exactly as crab crew do (drawn from her own document's tables; poses the document lacks fall back to the walk frames). Default false: her register's refuseHire line stands. walkins: this people's share of anonymous walk-ins and migrated-save seeding, in TWENTIETHS (0-8; 0 = never, the default and byte-identical to today - the roll is skipped entirely, no draw). Ownership of a declared business binds to a settler in a later slice.

rhythm.description: Census C1 (R0-R2 live): when this people sleep and work, relative to the world's one sun - darkness() never moves; a nocturnal culture moves its bodies, not the sky. Integer game-minutes on the 30-minute grain (17:00 = 1020). wake/bed: the sleeping arc's ends; bed may be earlier than wake (the awake arc wraps midnight). What is clamped is the DERIVED awake arc: 8h-20h on the 24h circle, checked AFTER field-by-field inheritance from the crab day (wake 450, bed 1260, lieIn 570, shiftStarts D 510 / M 480 / E 840, hours 480-1200) - a partial declaration that composes into an insane day is refused by name at install ('A DAY WITH NO NIGHT', 'A PEOPLE WHO NEVER WAKE', 'A SHIFT IN THEIR SLEEP', 'A LIE-IN IN THEIR SLEEP'). lieIn: a resident's day-off rise. shiftStarts: where D/M/E clock-ins anchor for shops this culture's settlers OWN (ends derive as start + management.shifts span; institutions follow their owner, bodies follow their culture, the town square follows the host). hours: the default sign a declared business opens with (owner lever thereafter); must satisfy the engine's sign rail (open < close, >= 4h, not before 6:00) - a sign across midnight is refused by name until the hours model learns to wrap (R3). Visitor bed/wake and the ferry trap are R3; nothing here reads them yet.

cards.description: Phase D (declarative cards): dossier cards a culture declares, up to 4. Each binds row labels to REGISTERED observables - the same versioned registry brains declare inputs from (need.thirst.q20, wallet.cents, ...). The first card renders on the visitor dossier with live values; an unknown observable is refused by name at import. Data reading data: no code, no draws, view-only.

obs.description: a registered observable name; the engine validator is the authority on the live set

manner.description: Census C4: how this people carries itself. speed: a visitor's stroll in px/s (crab: 42) - the stepper, the JS reference, AND the ferry ETA all read the same dispatched value, so a slow culture is never promised a boat it cannot catch. stroll: how far one stroll wanders in px (crab: 340); the promenade band itself (VIS_ROAM) is the town's geography and stays engine. space: personal-space radius in px (crab: 8, RULED on a measured growth curve - declaring wider buys the same detour tax that cost 5 escapes in 48 at 10px; capped at 16 so no document can gridlock a counter; a mixed pair parts to the LARGER radius, give_berth's own max rule). walkMul20: a settled resident's gait in twentieths (20 = the crab pace), composing with the trait multiplier. rides: may this people take the buggy - REFUSED true until a culture-ride art seam exists (the buggy art indexes crab colorways); false is the settlers walk pin, as data. Fields left out inherit the crab values.

body.description: Census C2, THE CULTURAL BODY: per-need decay-rate and want-threshold multipliers in TWENTIETHS (20 = 1x the crab constants; converted once at install, ROUND-HALF-UP, so all-20s is byte-identical to declaring nothing). rates: how fast each need accrues - per-field 10-40 (0.5x-2.0x), and the five rates together may not sum past 120 (mean 1.2x): inflating every need mints spend from a text file, so the aggregate is the cheat gate (A BODY TOO HUNGRY FOR THE PIER). wants: how full a need must be before a guest acts, 10-30 twentieths of the crab thresholds. The need SET is the engine's five, always - a key this body does not have is refused. Resident tired COSTS (shift, errand, nightfall) ride the tired multiplier; recovery (bed, cot, nap, the sand's 3/2) stays the engine's - WHERE you sleep, not WHO you are.

foodways.description: Phase B (LIVE 2026-08-22): dishes in BIZ-shaped rows a kitchen here can LEARN - author-side whole dollars crossing the cents boundary at load, ingredients priced through the import machinery (nothing conjured), items carrying their own 9-wide pixel art on the global palette. The demand must be TAUGHT (a departure card with a foreign settle) before the manage card offers the lesson.

ingredients.description: A culture's own priced imports, joining the pier's list at install (author whole dollars per unit; the cent is born at ingredientCost). May not re-price the native pantry (fish_raw, fruit, token, soap, linen) nor an ingredient another installed culture already priced. Max 16.

id.description: must not shadow the house menu's own recipe ids

biz.description: a kitchen business that exists; every step's station must exist there

icon.description: a native item or one declared in items{} with art

pay.description: author dollars; the cent is born at menuPrice

learn.description: one-time lesson fee in author dollars (0 = free)

raw.description: an ingredient the trade machinery prices (INGREDIENT_COST)

prefixItems.description: item carried out of the step

items.description: display names + optional 9-wide pixel art (global palette chars, '.' transparent); may not shadow the native pantry

businesses.description: Phase B (FORMAT LIVE 2026-08-22): whole shops a culture declares - catalog SUBSTANCE only (recipes, stations as TYPE+capacity, economics in author dollars). Never map coordinates (placement is the town's, phase D) and never an owner (ownership binds to a settler when settlers exist). A declared business is built and PENDING - inspectable, not placed - until a plot exists. Max 4.

kind.description: one of the town building templates; a new kind needs world art first (the world section, reserved)

rent.description: author dollars per day; cents at build

wage.description: this shop's advertised wage in author dollars; omitted = the town rate (WAGE_STD) when placed

lodging.description: stalls are ROOMS kept until morning (the hotel bit)

sellable.description: grows an OFFER chip when placed and NPC-owned

stations.description: station TYPE -> working capacity (1-4). Coordinates are the town map, never the culture.

source.description: the station where raws enter; must be one of stations

out.description: the pass; must be one of stations

id.description: must not shadow the house menu's own recipe ids

icon.description: a native item or one declared in items{} with art

pay.description: author dollars; the cent is born at menuPrice

learn.description: one-time lesson fee in author dollars (0 = free)

raw.description: an ingredient the trade machinery prices (INGREDIENT_COST)

prefixItems.description: item carried out of the step

items.description: The BIZ recipe shape, validated by the same recipeRowProblem as foodway dishes; steps' stations resolve against this business's own declared stations.

conduct.description: Layer-0 rule table (proposal); Layer-1 expressions join per-field when a rule needs a formula.

civics.description: Phase E4 - HOW THIS PEOPLE'S VOTERS SCORE A PLATFORM, and (slice 4a) THE BALLOT DIALS a mayor sets. stakes: platValue (the number an election ranks a policy by, for one voter) re-expressed as a list of NAMED Layer-1 term-programs, the platform's value the SUM (family 1). The engine owns the id space: the 'platform' stake is REQUIRED (a section that omits it is refused - it would silently fall back to the engine lambda), and a term reads the platform-value bundle by name (potStake20 pBowls roofWeight20 roof fr fb capStake100 purseCost100 pTake). Each term is a straight-line program (see the MCP op table) that CLOSES WITH TERM; a term is SIGNED (negative bounds are fine - floorBill and purseCost subtract), only the 2^52 magnitude rail applies. An undeclared civics section leaves this people's voters on the engine's own lambda, byte-identical to today. ballots: the two TOWN-LEVEL dials (the wage floor and the house limit) as step-ladders - see the ballots property. purses: the four purses that fund the shelter (levy/dues/rents/tin) as rate grids - see the purses property. calendar: the polling clock (pollWeekday/pollOpen/pollShut) as scalars - see the calendar property. relief: the shelter and soup terms as scalars - see the relief property. eligibility: the two franchise predicates (who may vote/stand) as 0/1 Layer-1 programs, dispatched per voter like stakes - see the eligibility property. All five civics families (stakes, ballots, purses, calendar, relief) plus eligibility are now authorable.

ballots.description: Phase E4 slice 4a - THE BALLOT DIALS a mayor sets and a voter prices, as step-ladders. Two dials: 'floor' (the wage floor, cents a day) and 'cap' (the house limit, employees a shop). Each is { id, name, short, unit, who, steps[] }. steps IS the ladder and the INDEX is what a save stores (hall.policy.cap = 4 is the INDEX of the 6-head rung, not six heads), so STEP 0 IS THE FOUNDING NO-POLICY (NO FLOOR / NO LIMIT - what every pre-feature save loads as) and must stay index 0 forever: the ladder EXTENDS, it never deletes step 0 (Matt's ruling 4, 2026-08-24). Every step is a whole count >= 0. These are TOWN-LEVEL (one town, one floor, one limit), so unlike stakes they are not dispatched per voter; the crab's own bundle adopts them in place and the engine literal is the fallback for a culture that declares none.

id.description: The dial id. 'floor' (wage floor) and 'cap' (house limit) are the engine's own.

name.description: The dial's full name on the campaign card.

unit.description: What a step counts (e.g. '$ A DAY, LOWEST PAID').

steps.description: The ladder, low to high. steps[0] MUST be 0 (the founding no-policy). A save stores the index, never the value.

purses.description: Phase E4 slice 4b - THE PURSES that fund the shelter, as rate grids. Five mechs (the engine's own id space): 'levy' (a share of every business's takings), 'dues' (a charge per visitor the ferry lands), 'rents' (a cut of Mr. Pincherton's house rents), 'tin' (a voluntary collection), 'tariff' (a duty on the landed price of imported goods, off the till that buys them). Each is { id, name, short, unit, who, steps[] }. steps IS the rate grid and the INDEX (0..4) is what a save stores, so STEP 0 IS NO TAKE (rate 0 raises nothing), the founding grid. Every step is a whole count >= 0 (percent for levy/rents/tariff, cents for dues/tin). Like the ballot dials these are TOWN-LEVEL, so the crab's own bundle adopts them in place and the engine literal is the fallback; the levy's conflict-of-interest and the conservation math stay engine.

id.description: The purse mech id. levy/dues/rents/tin/tariff are the engine's own.

unit.description: What a step counts (e.g. '% OF TAKINGS', '$ A HEAD').

steps.description: The rate grid, low to high. steps[0] MUST be 0 (NO TAKE). A save stores the index, never the value.

calendar.description: Phase E4 slice 4c - THE POLLING CLOCK, as scalars. pollWeekday is the weekday INDEX (0..6; 6 = Sunday, the town's own week - polling day rides that rather than inventing a second calendar). pollOpen/pollShut are MINUTES past midnight (default 420/1140 - the polls open an hour before the town and shut an hour before it, so a working crab's vote is sometimes tight). TOWN-LEVEL, adopted in place; the const literal is the fallback. Missing fields are fine (the crab's own bundle carries them). POLL_PLACES geometry, VOTE_SECS, and the ballot logistics stay engine.

pollWeekday.description: The weekday index polling day falls on (0=Mon .. 6=Sun).

pollOpen.description: Minutes past midnight the polls open (default 420 = 07:00).

pollShut.description: Minutes past midnight the polls shut (default 1140 = 19:00). Must be after pollOpen.

relief.description: Phase E4 slice 4c - THE SHELTER AND THE SOUP, as scalars. These sit on STATE and TIME paths (a pot is spent, the shelter charges rent and bolts after strikes, reopens after shutNights), so a transcription must be byte-equal AND wired - the behaviour gate proves the paths fire on these numbers. TOWN-LEVEL, adopted in place; the const literals are the fallback. NOTE soup.potMax is also the stakes lcm denominator, so a different value would desync the platform valuation. Conservation (fundTake/Pay/Remit) and the strike-counter mechanism stay engine.

potMax.description: The most bowls a mayor may put on for one night (default 6). Also 345000 = D/(20*potMax) in the stakes lcm.

margin.description: The shack's margin on a bowl sold to the town, in CENTS (default 200).

rent.description: Mr. Pincherton's nightly charge for the shelter, in CENTS (default 1000).

float.description: How many nights of rent the purse is struck to carry in hand (default 1).

strikes.description: Missed nights running before the door is bolted (default 3).

shutNights.description: How many nights the door stays bolted (default 4).

eligibility.description: Phase E4 slice 4d - THE FRANCHISE (family 2: who may). Two 0/1 PREDICATE programs over the persona read bundle (npc/owner/homeless), NOT tables. vote: who may cast a ballot (the crab's is [["PUSHI",1]] - every resident votes; the visitor is excluded structurally). stand: who may put themselves forward (the crab's is [["LD","npc"]] - only townsfolk self-nominate; the player's crew stand only by nomination). Each is a bare Layer-1 program (the depart weight/select shape, NOT TERM-closed) whose static bound must lie in [0,1] - a program that could return anything else is not a predicate and is refused. PER-VOTER, so it dispatches on the voter's culture like stakes; a culture that declares none leaves its residents on the engine's inlined gates, byte-identical. Both keys are required (the engine reads both).

vote.description: A 0/1 Layer-1 predicate over the persona bundle: who may vote.

stand.description: A 0/1 Layer-1 predicate over the persona bundle: who may self-nominate.

stakes.description: The signed value-terms a voter sums to score a platform. Must include the 'platform' stake (the engine's own).

id.description: The stake id. 'platform' is the engine's own and is required.

terms.description: Named signed value-terms; the stake's value is their sum.

name.description: The term name - unique within the stake; the receipt reads off the largest-magnitude term.

prog.description: A straight-line Layer-1 program over the platform-value bundle that CLOSES WITH TERM. Signed; only the 2^52 magnitude rail applies.

depart.description: Departure-card rule re-weighting (registry row 4) and, since phase E3, the full rule table as Layer-1 programs. weights: ruleId -> integer 0..8, a QUARTERS multiplier on the engine's rule weight (4 = identity, 0 = silence the rule for this people, 8 = twice as loud). Unknown rule ids are refused at import. rules: ALL-OR-NOTHING re-expression of every engine departure rule - weights are compared across rules in one scaled space (each weight program computes 300 * purse * w), so a table missing a rule is refused by name. Each rule: id (an engine rule id), optional mood (sour/flat/mixed/glad/made), weight (a straight-line Layer-1 program over the depart read bundle - see the MCP op table - whose static bound must be non-negative), line.select (a program whose static bound must land inside line.templates), line.templates (1-8 strings, max 120 chars, speaking through the departure slot engine: WHY NIGHTS QUITS TABLES DUES PAID TOPBIZ LIST plus the phase C slots).
